place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 240, 244, 245 & 251, 240 Birch Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; built 1934: a hipped roof, a tall exterior chimney, twin entrances with a canted bay and small hood, a big glazed sunporch at one side and a wooden fence behind.

floors: W W W W W W
facade.notes: a hip-roofed brick duplex (1934) with a pedimented double entry, a tall end chimney, an enclosed sunroom; a wooden privacy fence round the back yard

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
